en: Having prostrated before the Goddess of Learning, who dwells within the lotus-like words of the Omniscient One, [I compose] the *Vajjālagga*.

I shall speak the "Dhammāiti" group of verses, which are well-spoken and consist of excellent knowledge. (1) How are those not ashamed who, having neither read nor heard Prakrit poetry—which is like nectar—yet claim to possess the true essence of love? (2)
Having selected the finest verses composed by various poets, this work named *Jayavallabha*, known as the *Vajjālagga*, was composed by Vīraka according to the rules.

That work in which ancient verses (paurāṇa-gāthās) are recited in a single arrangement is indeed called the *Vajjālagga*; furthermore, it is said that "vajja" refers to a sequence (paddhati). He who always recites this entire *Vajjālagga* at the appropriate occasion... [4] // Vajjālagga 4 // ...[he attains... He shall become a poet of Prakrit verse and likewise illustrious. (5) // VajLag.5 // [The Pathway of the Listener Free from Sorrow]

When it is being performed for those who are already content, listeners are difficult to find.
